Both search variants are verified and working. They share your saved links, so you'll see the same bookmarks in each. **If your list is short right now, save a few links first** so the search has something to work with.

Here are the two versions to compare — they're identical except for one thing: **how the search runs.**

- **Version A — filters instantly as you type:**
  **http://maker:4001/find-a-instant.html**
  Type part of a word (e.g. `css`, or `web`) and watch the list narrow with each keystroke. Delete the text to see everything return.

- **Version B — type, then press Enter or the Search button:**
  **http://maker:4001/find-b-button.html**
  Type a word or two (e.g. `linux kernel`), then press Enter or click **Search**. The list only updates when you run it. Use **Clear** to reset.

**Which of these two feels right for finding a link quickly?** Try the same search in both so you can feel the difference.

Two things I set up the *same* in both (please check these are right, since they're not what's being compared):

- **What search looks through:** each link's title, description, *and* web address — so you can find something by any of those.
- **Multiple words:** if you type more than one word, a link has to contain *all* of them to show up (typing `linux kernel` finds only links containing both). Is that the behaviour you'd want, or should any one of the words be enough?
